items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Now, it was run by an old man they called Pop Pearson and his son, Charlie.

ctx.x: Oh ... there was a club, not a club, but a little place, a little dancehall -- like I said, I wasn't quite 14, and I was working in this club, and it was a little dancehall right down the 30th block on Cosgrove called The Vipers. Now, it was run by an old man they called Pop Pearson and his son, Charlie. Well, Charlie had -- to me, I

believe that was the first stereo -- he made a vendor, and played records -- he had about 6 or 7 loud speakers, and he built it, and he'd sit up there and work the controls, and he knew all the arrangements, these big bands, and certain bands he would turn it up, you know, turn the volume up, and oh, it was so beautiful -- it was just like being -- sitting up close to a big band.
